tagline: Up Cedar Canyon to the lava country and a leaking lake.
intro: SR 14 leaves Cedar City through its red hill and a forest of maple and scrub oak, then climbs on grades of more than 8 percent through Cedar Canyon onto the Markagunt Plateau. It twists through aspen and pine along the plateau's edge, tops out at 9,900 feet a mile short of the Cedar Breaks turnoff, and runs east over ancient lava fields before it comes down into Long Valley at US 89.

The mountainsides here do not always hold still. In October 2011 a mountainside gave way near mile marker 8 and took about 1,300 feet of road with it, and the highway stayed closed for more than seven months.

moments.title: Cedar Canyon
moments.text: The road climbs a narrow canyon with sheer cliffs towering on both sides, looking into the Ashdown Gorge Wilderness.

moments.title: Navajo Lake
moments.text: Around a sharp bend the overlook opens on a shallow lake dammed by a lava flow, which drains through sinkholes in its floor into the Great Basin and the Colorado River both.

moments.title: Duck Creek Village
moments.text: A summer hamlet at 8,507 feet on the edge of Cedar Mountain, with a Forest Service visitor center at Duck Creek Pond that keeps summer hours only.

practical: Vehicles over 12 feet wide or 65 feet long are prohibited on the climb, and anything over 8.5 feet wide needs pilot escorts. Services along the way are very limited.
